criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately follows the operative governance record (record-17.txt, which is approved and in force per registry.txt) by requiring Finance controllers, Program Managers, and Purchase approval for every price change request, while rejecting the unapproved draft in record-22.txt. It also preserves all baseline TRSO and nomination signoff authorities from the request and clearly frames the workflow as a proposed future-state blueprint rather than an active override of existing controls.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
evidence.output_quote: Price-change gate: every price change request requires Finance controllers, Program Managers and Purchase approval, including changes calculated from agreed module rates.

evidence.source_quote: Price change request approvals: Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams. All three are required.
evidence.output_quote: Price-change gate: every price change request requires Finance controllers, Program Managers and Purchase approval, including changes calculated from agreed module rates.

evidence.source_quote: TRSOs are reviewed and signed off by ER, Quality, and Purchase teams.
evidence.output_quote: ER prepares the TRSO using Program and market inputs. ER, Quality and Purchase sign the same version.

evidence.source_quote: The final step is a formal supplier nomination, which must be documented with a full record of communication trails, negotiation summaries, internal evaluations, and signoffs from Finance, Quality, ER, and Program Managers.
evidence.output_quote: Purchase compiles the recommendation and complete approval file. Obtain Finance, Quality, ER and Program signoffs on the same package.

criteria.consequence: None; operative governance rules and role signoffs are accurately preserved.
criteria.counterevidence: None found; record-22.txt states 'Price change request approval: Purchase team alone.', which registry.txt explicitly marks as an unapproved draft.

criteria.rationale: The Word document fulfills all elements of the CPO's brief: it defines the modular quotation structure across features, design elements, child parts, and raw materials; specifies baseline sourcing steps, decision gates, evaluation criteria, and approval layers; establishes fast-path and exception-path mechanisms for post-nomination lamp design changes; and provides a clear digital platform blueprint and governance plan for both the CPO and TechSol.

evidence.source_quote: Revised sourcing and nomination workflow must involve a ‘Modular quotation structure’ to develop a plug-and-play model for cost drivers based on features, design elements, child parts and raw material used. Clearly define the process steps, decision gates, approval layers, and flexibility points to handle post-nomination design changes.
evidence.output_quote: Structure it as a base assembly plus selectable feature, design-element, child-part and raw-material modules.

evidence.source_quote: Once approved, your team identifies potential suppliers and evaluates them on multiple factors — including technical competency, manufacturing capability, cost competitiveness, reliability, localization potential, and quality systems.
evidence.output_quote: Purchase coordinates a documented comparison of technical competency, manufacturing capability, cost competitiveness, reliability, localization potential and quality systems.

evidence.source_quote: In response, the CPO has tasked you with drafting a revised sourcing workflow that introduces greater agility, allowing the purchase process to adapt flexibly to late-stage design changes without compromising traceability, stakeholder visibility, or project governance.
evidence.output_quote: Configuration fast path: use existing modules only when specifications, compatibility, commercial validity and capacity assumptions remain applicable. Generate the configuration comparison and cost bridge automatically. Reuse unaffected evidence by reference and obtain signoff on affected TRSO content from ER, Quality and Purchase.

evidence.source_quote: As a first step, the CPO has asked you to develop the first-level workflow draft for this new sourcing process — both as a strategic process recommendation and as the foundational blueprint for the digital platform the TechSol will build.
evidence.output_quote: Create linked records for program, part/variant, supplier, TRSO, assessment, RFQ, module catalogue, quotation, negotiation, nomination and change request.

criteria.consequence: None; the deliverable is complete and ready for executive and technical review.

task_defect.reason: The request and workspace records are unambiguous and internally consistent regarding which governance record is operative.

assessment.caveat: No weighted average can offset a critical failure. Exact quotes establish traceability, not entailment. Rendering and independent human calibration remain required.
